quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. A locked rear wheel on an upright motorcycle going straight usually does not cause loss of control.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left track is often safest.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead of you.
Stay closer behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road.

questions.question: After passing in a group, the lead rider should move into:

options.text: The right portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The left portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: After passing, the lead rider should return to the left portion of the lane. Moving to the right portion can encourage the next rider to pass before it is safe.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
The sun is shining.
You believe stopping will be routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if the pavement is slippery and your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Also increase following distance if you cannot see ahead clearly or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to turn.
Do not drag your feet on the road.
Avoid looking at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always scan for other traffic. Slow before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Never drag your feet on the road.

questions.question: One of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on, including your high beam during the day and night when legal and safe.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.

options.text: The left portion
The middle portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center portion of a lane.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Someone is following you too closely.
You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others will notice. This is especially important when slowing down faster than expected.

questions.question: Tell your passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to wait until after you start the engine before getting on. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: An engine seizes because of:

options.text: Not enough oil.
Not enough fuel.
Wrong tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil is low. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot slide smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position. Good riders change their position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet when riding?

options.text: All motorcycle passengers
Motorcycle passengers under age 21
Motorcycle passengers riding with a new rider
No one

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle passengers under age 21
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, all riders and passengers under age 21 must wear helmets and eye protection. Helmets and eye protection are strongly recommended for all riders.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Does not mean they will yield to you properly.
Guarantees they will yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully near intersections. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes so you can respond quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should be used at all times.
Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is generally good, but switch to single-file when riding curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can best see and be seen.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can best see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Adjust your position in the lane to see better and be more visible. For a left turn, stay to the right to see oncoming traffic. For a right turn, stay left-center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit with your arms straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance.

questions.question: When positioning your body on the motorcycle:

options.text: Hold yourself up with your arms.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down at the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over scored pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center portion of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in the rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give an emergency vehicle extra space and proceed with caution. Always slow down and be ready to stop when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Shift down to a lower gear right away.
Ride in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.
Relax and steer straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over uneven bridge gratings, simply relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Steering side to side is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog get closer, then speed up and leave it behind.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get closer, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If chased by a dog, slow down and let it approach. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be at the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should be placed near the front of the group, behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Recommended but not required.
Only required for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear DOT-approved helmets every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a surface with good grip, you should:

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear tire on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control the motorcycle on a good surface as long as it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least this distance behind another vehicle:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. Use a larger distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on every ride.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Always wear hearing protection when riding.
